criteria.name: Iterable vs element reads without a legend
This-turn vs next-turn reads without a legend
Survives more than one carried value

A.name: As drawn
A.one_line: Your drawing with the geometry tightened — the control everything else is measured against.

B.name: Split-face wall port
B.one_line: One dot, painted as its two faces: filled outside, hollow inside, with the type change written across it.

C.name: Row-aligned item
C.one_line: The boundary port sits at the row it feeds, so the item cable is one short horizontal run and nothing crosses.

D.name: Seed named on the back cable
D.one_line: The z⁻¹ chip states both facts a delay has: one step late, and what arrives first.

E.name: The zero-iterations cable
E.one_line: Draws what the analyzer already derives: if the loop never runs, estimate()'s pose is what leaves.

F.name: Back cable on the floor
F.one_line: The return is not a free cable — it rides the region's own bottom border.

G.name: Tight stub
G.one_line: The shortest possible return: out of the block, under it, and straight back in.

H.name: Weight change, no pill
H.one_line: The cable outside is a doubled rail; it becomes a single rail at the wall. The pill is deleted.

I.name: Binding pill
I.one_line: The pill stops being an index and becomes the Python binding itself.

J.name: Live values
J.one_line: Every mark carries the value it actually has this turn.

B: The split dot is untouched by a second carry — it says one thing about one collection and stays out of the way.
C: Row alignment is what makes two lanes survive: with the item cable out of the vertical channel, both back cables get a clean floor lane.
J: Two live chips plus a live item pill is three moving strings on one board. It reads, but it is the first thing to switch off.

S2.title: the carry is written by a different block

B: Nothing about the boundary changes when the body grows; the split dot is a statement about the collection, not about the body.
C: The long back cable is now the ONLY right-to-left line on the board, which is exactly what makes it readable at a glance.
J: The best showing of the three: `z⁻¹ = pose₂` names the value at the far end of a long cable, where the reader has lost track of it.

S3.title: a carry and a collection leaving together

B: The wall now carries one marked port and two unmarked exits. The asymmetry invites the question the split dot cannot answer: is `trail` one float or many?
C: Nothing changes for C — its whole claim is about the inbound side, and the two exits stay clear of it.
J: `z⁻¹ = pose₂` beside a live `score()` output is exactly the distinction the reader needs: one is last turn's, one is this turn's.

S4.title: a carry that is not written every turn

B: A port that says `Poses → Pose` says nothing about a turn that produces no write. The split dot is silent exactly where the reader needs a word.
C: Same silence. Routing cannot express a conditional write, and the guard band is drawn here rather than modelled.
J: The only one that can speak: the chip reads `z⁻¹ = pose₂ (unchanged)` on a skipped turn, which is the fact and nothing else. This is the case that earns live values their place.

B: The inner region needs its own boundary port, and its collection is `track.dets` — an attribute of the outer element, not an outer input. The split dot has no way to say where its collection came from.
C: Two regions, two row-aligned entries, two floor lanes and not one crossing. Row alignment is what stops nesting turning into a knot.
J: Correct but crowded: five live strings on one board, and the inner chip's value changes several times per outer turn, which no static reading can follow.
